label: Figure 4.3: The demand for bus passes (inelastic, revenue rises)
alt: A downward-sloping demand curve for bus passes with shaded revenue areas a, b and c. Price rises from $50 to $60 and quantity falls from 10,000 to 9,000.
caption: The price of a monthly bus pass rises from $50 to $60 and quantity demanded falls from 10,000 to 9,000, so PED = −10% ÷ +20% = −0.5 (inelastic). Area c ($50 × 1,000 = $50,000) is lost, but area a ($10 × 9,000 = $90,000) is gained. Because a is larger than c, total revenue rises by $40,000, from $500,000 to $540,000.
